name: Apache Commons BCEL
purpose: Manipulate Java class files as symbolic objects.
inputs: Binary JVM class files or programmatically assembled class descriptions.
action: Read, transform, create and write classes with methods, fields and instructions. JustIce reports verification problems.
constraints: Class-file and JVM scope. The overview gives no guarantee about individual transforms.

name: Apache Commons BeanUtils
purpose: Access Java bean properties dynamically.
inputs: JavaBeans with conventional getters and setters and names supplied at runtime.
action: Wrap reflection and introspection, including dynamic property access for template and script consumers.
constraints: The 2.x package namespace changes and is binary incompatible with 1.x.

name: Apache Bean Scripting Framework
purpose: Embed a scripting language in a Java application.
inputs: Installed scripting engines and bound Java objects.
action: Invoke scripting engines from Java and register objects for script access.
constraints: BSF 2.x uses its own API. The 3.x API is JSR-223 and engine availability varies.

name: Apache Commons CLI
purpose: Parse application command-line options and print help.
inputs: A Java application's argument vector and declared options.
action: Read POSIX, GNU, Java-property and attached-value short options. Format example usage.
constraints: The overview's option list gives no behavior for malformed combinations. CLI 2 was never released.

name: Apache Commons Codec
purpose: Reuse common encoders and decoders.
inputs: Bytes or strings appropriate to Base64, hex, phonetic or URL codecs.
action: Provide concrete encoding and decoding utilities with an abstract codec framework.
constraints: Historical Base64 forks differed in RFC 2045 compliance. The overview gives no cross-codec round-trip guarantee.

name: Apache Commons Collections
purpose: Extend the Java collection interfaces and utilities.
inputs: Java objects, maps, sequences or collection wrappers.
action: Provide counted bags, bidirectional lookup, insertion-order maps, transforming decorators and composite views.
constraints: Individual structures have distinct semantics. Insertion-time transformation changes the object stored.

name: Apache Commons Compress
purpose: Handle Java archive and compression formats.
inputs: Compressed streams or archives containing entries for files or directories.
action: Separate single-stream compressors from structured multi-entry archivers.
constraints: Read and write support depends on format. Some codecs depend on other libraries and the documented release requires Java 8.

name: Apache Commons Configuration
purpose: Read typed Java configuration from multiple sources.
inputs: Properties, XML, INI, plist, JDBC, JNDI, system and other configuration sources.
action: Use builders and a combined configuration to mix sources and retrieve typed single or multiple values.
constraints: Migrating from 1.x to 2.x requires changed imports and possibly other changes.

name: Generating JSON from Tabular Data on the Web
purpose: Convert annotated tables into JSON using defined mapping rules.
inputs: Rows, cells and CSVW annotations for names, links and datatypes.
action: Produce minimal row objects or standard table objects. Nest objects and handle typed values and skipped output.
constraints: JSON omits certain absent values. The algorithm works on the annotated model and governs conversion output.

name: Generating RDF from Tabular Data on the Web
purpose: Convert annotated tabular data into RDF.
inputs: CSVW table groups with row and column annotations and optional URI templates.
action: Generate subject-predicate-object statements and optionally include provenance in standard output.
constraints: Minimal and standard output differ. The destination is an RDF graph and some typed mappings require special handling.

name: Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
purpose: Describe tabular data for validation, conversion, display and search.
inputs: JSON metadata for table groups, tables, columns and dialects.
action: Assign canonical names and language-tagged titles. Set virtual columns, suppression, datatypes, delimiters and header counts.
constraints: Invalid property shapes have warning or ignore rules. Some names are reserved and headers can override boolean flags.

name: Model for Tabular Data and Metadata on the Web
purpose: Represent and process annotated tabular data.
inputs: Rows, columns, raw cell strings and metadata such as datatype, default, separator and null indicators.
action: Maintain raw and typed cell values plus errors. Parse and validate keys and cells.
constraints: The model discards CSV quoting distinctions. Missing strings may map to null. Some validation errors halt processing.

name: CSV on the Web A Primer
purpose: Explain CSVW metadata through practical examples.
inputs: CSV plus JSON annotations for types, defaults, keys, names and output choices.
action: Show typed validation, omission and defaulting of missing values, suppressing columns, and nested conversion.
constraints: A Working Group Note. An invalid numeric default in its example becomes a string.

name: CSV on the Web Use Cases and Requirements
purpose: Document tabular interoperability use cases and requirements.
inputs: Real scenarios such as transferring record descriptions or previewing CSV in a browser.
action: Describe hierarchies using row identifiers and discuss preprocessing, dialects, type detection and display.
constraints: A Working Group Note with accepted, partial and deferred requirements. A use case gives no implementation guarantee.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Structured Data Calendars
purpose: Identify what to preserve when migrating calendars.
inputs: Calendar entries, schedules, attendee roles, reminders and attached data.
action: Prioritize structure including entry and user relationships, recurrence, time zones, participation and property parameters.
constraints: Text styling normally has low priority unless significant to a record. Federal archival guidance is tied to preservation.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Structured Data Databases
purpose: Preserve the meaningful structure and interaction context of database records.
inputs: Database records plus schema, encoding and application metadata.
action: Record structure, relationships and metadata so users can understand fields and potentially recreate interactions such as queries.
constraints: Format availability depends on transfer and access setting. Recreating prior software interactions is conditional.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Digital Audio
purpose: Preserve meaningful properties of audio recordings during migration.
inputs: Digital audio with channels, sampling, bit depth, timing and technical metadata.
action: Track structure and playback characteristics. Preserve administrative and technical metadata inline or as sidecar.
constraints: Embedded and external metadata need association. Format choices and preservation fidelity depend on source and holdings.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Digital Cinema
purpose: Preserve films as digital cinema records.
inputs: Moving images, audio, aspect ratio, bit depth, frame rate and technical metadata.
action: Retain appearance, channel and ordering characteristics plus contextual information inline or in a sidecar.
constraints: Original media integrity limits color reproduction. Transfer and public-access formats follow different lists.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Digital Design and Vector Graphics
purpose: Preserve essential visual and functional characteristics in design migration.
inputs: Design records with vector geometry, layers, rendering attributes and format metadata.
action: Retain relevant overlay, display and structural distinctions so parts can still be interpreted.
constraints: Exact colors may be unattainable. Distinctions can still be significant in query results.

name: NARA Preservation Action Plan for Digital Still Image
purpose: Preserve meaningful appearance and context for digital still images.
inputs: Raster images with pixels, color, resolution, bit depth and metadata.
action: Retain characteristics used in displaying and interpreting the image, and match transfer format to record type.
constraints: Preferred formats differ across born-digital, digitized paper and digitized photos. Lossy changes affect fidelity.
